subject: Selection for Cost Governance Tool - sourcing and next steps
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Cost governance tooling — shortlist & ask

Team —

Following the FinOps review last week, we need to pick a primary cost governance vendor to replace our aging internal dashboards. I pulled together three finalists based on scale, visibility and automation capabilities: FinSightOps, CloudEconomix, and ThriftyOps.

High-level asks:
- Can we validate product fit against the attached Cost-Gov Requirements checklist (short list below)?
- Recommend which vendor we should prioritize for an executive demo/pilot next week.
- Flag any procurement / legal blockers early (e.g., data residency, SOC2 evidence).

Key checklist highlights (attached): asset tagging reconciliation, cross-account budget enforcement, anomaly detection with alerting, prefix-based cost allocation, sandboxed cost simulations for rollouts.

I've cc'd procurement to formalize SOW expectations after we pick a vendor. Please reply with short bullets by EOD Monday so we can lock demos for the following week.

Thanks,
Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Head of Cloud Economics | Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0142

Attachment: Cost-Gov-Requirements-Checklist.xlsx
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cost governance tooling — shortlist & ask

Naomi — quick initial pass below. I ran the three vendors through the internal scoring template (security, ops integration, cost visibility, automation). Short version:

- FinSightOps (Claudia) — strongest on anomaly detection and ML-driven forecasts; good API parity; pricing is premium but early pilot references are solid.
- CloudEconomix (sales@cloudeconomix.com) — best UI and tagging reconciliation; slower on multi-account enforcement; cheaper.
- ThriftyOps (partners@thriftyops.io) — focused on cost-savings automation (rightsizing/spot filling); good TCO play for sustained savings but less mature on governance policies.

Recommendation: prioritize FinSightOps for an executive pilot to validate forecasting accuracy + anomaly catching. Run a parallel small integration POC with CloudEconomix focused on tagging reconciliation.

Open Qs:
1) Does FinSightOps' model require any data export outside our VPC? Security will need to validate.
2) What pilot size do we propose (10 accounts / 3 months?)

I can own the POC plan if you want me to coordinate vendors and metrics.

-Ben
Ben Carter
Principal Infrastructure Engineer
ben_carter@redwood.com

From: Claudia Ruiz <claudia@finsightops.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: sales@cloudeconomix.com
Date: Mon, 4 Oct 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cost governance tooling — shortlist & ask

Hi Naomi & Ben —

Thanks for considering FinSightOps. Attaching our updated proposal and a short pilot plan. Quick answers up front: we can run the forecasting models entirely on a customer-hosted gateway (no raw cost data leaves your VPC), and we have a SOC2 Type II report we can share under NDA.

Pilot suggestion (fast track):
- Scope: 12 accounts (non-prod + core infra), 8-week pilot with weekly checkpoints.
- Success metrics: 95% anomaly precision, forecast MAE < 5% over 30-day horizon, automated cost alerts reduced alert noise by 40%.
- Deliverables: initial connector, dashboard templates, scripted runbook for remediation actions.

Available demo slots next week: Tue 10/6 11am PT, Wed 10/7 2pm PT. I've attached the proposal PDF and a short case study.

Attachment: FinSightOps-Proposal-Redwood-20261004.pdf

Happy to run the demo and walk through the security controls.

Best,
Claudia Ruiz
Head of Partnerships, FinSightOps
claudia@finsightops.com
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Claudia Ruiz <claudia@finsightops.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 4 Oct 2026 15:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cost governance tooling — shortlist & ask

Claudia — thanks for the quick turnaround and for clarifying the data residency point. That addresses a major procurement concern.

Internal: Laura/Evelyn — can you please:
- Laura: confirm procurement steps and target SOW timeline (we'd like to be execution-ready if the pilot goes well)
- Evelyn: please review the SOC2 note and tell us whether we need a formal security questionnaire answered before the demo.

Ben — I like your proposed split: FinSightOps for forecasting/policy, CloudEconomix for tagging POC. Let's lock FinSightOps for Wed 10/7 2pm PT. Claudia — please send a calendar invite and include a short pre-read.

Naomi

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 5 Oct 2026 15:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cost governance tooling — shortlist & ask

All — procurement next steps:

1) I'll draft a one-page SOW template for an 8-week pilot (deliverables, acceptance criteria, payment milestones). I'll share by EOD Thu (attached: RACI-Cloud-Gov-draft.docx).
2) I'll open a sourcing packet and issue an NDA & supplier security checklist to FinSightOps today; once we have the completed questionnaire and SOC2 evidence we can push the PO path.
3) If the pilot meets acceptance, we'll run a 12-month pilot contract with an optional conversion credit for the pilot fee.

Action items:
- Naomi: confirm pilot account list (Ben to share)
- Ben: draft POC success metrics and instrumentation plan (I can fold into the SOW)
- Evelyn: if we need additional security review, compile the specific ask and I'll pause contract steps until resolved.

Attachments: RACI-Cloud-Gov-draft.docx

Laura Bennett
Senior Procurement Manager | Redwood Inference
